Hi Alice — thanks for the samples and the plan. Quick read-through and thoughts below. I'm including the criteria we typically recommend for an AB gate + a pragmatic fallback approach.

Proposed acceptance metrics (48-hour window):
- Quantitative:
  * CTR / Click-through: no statistically significant drop vs control (alpha=0.05, two-sided).
  * Hallucination proxy: flagged factual-assertion failures per 1k prompts — must be <= 1.5x control.
  * User-reported clarity / NPS pulse: mean survey score not lower than control by >0.3 points.
- Qualitative:
  * Top-20 sampled conversational threads reviewed by product & eval; show <= 2 high-severity hallucinations.
  * No P0 privacy/data-leak incidents.

Fast fallback options (engineer effort & tradeoffs):
- Prompt override (minutes): push a conservative system prompt that restricts assertions. Lowest effort but can reduce helpfulness.
- Pin previous promptset (hours): switch routing to the last-stable promptset version. Minimal risk, minor rollout ops.
- Model variant fallback (hours): switch to smaller model family that has previously been validated. Higher latency/cost tradeoff.

Owners I recommend:
- Grace: coordinate communication with Brightlytics and own go/no-go decision.
- Marissa: run qualitative sample review and sign off on dialogue examples.
- Karthik: own the rollback ops (prompt override + routing).
- Rishi: own eval gating and sample triage; produce a short incident report if we hit thresholds.
- Stephanie: monitor production signals and surface anomalies to SRE on-call.

I'll draft a one-page checklist we can send to Alice with links to the rollback playbook.

Marissa

Thanks — quick clarifications from infra/ops perspective:
1) Prompt override: we can push a config change to routing that sets a system prompt within ~10-30 minutes, but it only applies to newly routed sessions; the KV cache means some active sessions may continue with the previous prompt for a short window. We should include a TTL guidance in the runbook.
2) Pin previous promptset: requires a rollback of the routing config and a small canary (10% for 15 mins) before full cutover; engineers on-call should be available for that 30-60 minute ops window.
3) Model variant fallback: we can auto-route to a pre-provisioned small model pool, but cost will increase ~1.8x. We should list cost owner signoff as optional.

Operational asks:
- Please add a short checklist item to verify that prefix caching is flushed for affected clients if we need immediate consistency.
- If we do prompt override, I'll need a single canonical override text confirmed by Marissa.

I'll stand by; I can be on-call if we decide to do the rollback tonight.

Adding the eval / QA lens. I reviewed the promptset_ab_samples.csv and ran a quick auto-check against our hallucination-detector. Summary:
- Estimated hallucination proxy for A arm: 2.1 per 1k (control is 1.0 per 1k) — above our suggested 1.5x threshold.
- False positive rate on the detector is ~12% on these conversational prompts.

Recommendation:
- Short-term: hold the A arm at 25% traffic and add a human-in-the-loop sample check every 2 hours (Marissa + Brightlytics PM). If the 2 hour sample shows >3 high-severity hallucinations, trigger prompt override + pin previous promptset.
- Medium-term: run a focused evaluation job overnight applying the stronger hallucination filters and include 500 extra conversational samples. I'll post the job results to the Jira ticket by midday.

I'll prepare the sampling deck for the 2-hour cadence and a template for the incident summary.
